title: World Bank Indicators API (World Development Indicators and other databases)
questions: how does US GDP per capita compare with other G7 countries
health spending as a share of GDP across countries
life expectancy in the US versus peer countries

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (each returns one JSON page; save it under the name shown) and upload the files. Without the links: open https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/<INDICATOR>?locations=<ISO2 codes joined with ->, e.g. https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.PCAP.CD?locations=US-GB-DE, choose Download > CSV, unzip, and upload the API_<indicator>_DS2_*.csv file (wide format: one column per year).

cache.why: Small JSON queries; WDI is revised several times a year, so data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: World Bank datasets are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) unless a dataset says otherwise (World Bank Terms of Use for Datasets); redistribution is allowed with attribution. Some indicators carry third-party terms noted in their metadata (sourceOrganization).

notices: Data from the World Bank, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/legal/terms-conditions/datasets).
citation: World Bank, {dataset}, World Bank Indicators API (api.worldbank.org/v2), licensed CC BY 4.0, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Current US dollars, constant dollars or PPP? Cross-country level comparisons usually need PPP (e.g. NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD); growth uses constant-price series (...KD.ZG); current US$ (...CD) moves with exchange rates.
Which comparison countries (G7, OECD members, income group or region aggregate) and which years? The latest year is often missing for many countries.
